prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 topological classification of insulators, and for the first experimental observation of protected edge transport in HgTe quantum wells.

statement.case_for: Band topology is now an organising principle for electronic phases, and it has spread well beyond solids into photonics, cold atoms and mechanical metamaterials. The Kane-Mele proposal and Z2 classification are original and conceptually clean. Molenkamp's HgTe experiment gave a direct transport fingerprint (quantised edge conductance), so the prize would rest on a prediction that was observed, not on theory alone. Independent confirmation across materials and probes now spans well over a decade, the interpretation is stable and timing is, if anything, late. After reading the opening ballots I move my first choice from B029 to B041 because colleagues' arguments on attribution persuade me. The Kane-Mele paper is the theoretical origin of the field, and a configuration that leaves Mele out is harder to defend than one that leaves Xue out.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is real: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe state that Molenkamp's group observed, and Fu, Moore, Balents and others are central to the 3D story, none of whom can be named here. A three-person limit therefore forces a contestable choice, and some members may read the 2016 prize on topological phases of matter as having already covered the area. The compound entries also overlap (B029 and B045), so the committee should treat them as one story and not split it. In my own opening I left out Mele because I could not adjudicate his role from the supplied text. I now think that omission was the weaker position, but I hold the new allocation with only moderate confidence.

responses.point: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall proposal, Molenkamp's group gave the decisive HgTe/CdTe realisation, and Kane-Mele-Molenkamp is the cleanest three-person configuration from the supplied names.
responses.response: I agree and I am changing my position on this point. My opening B029 trio omitted Mele and added Xue, and I now see that Mele's role in the Z2 theory makes that the less defensible allocation. I do not share the view that Hasan's exclusion is a minor matter, because he has a strong 3D claim. But I think the 2D theory-plus-experiment story is the sharper and better-documented discovery, and I would rather defend that than dilute it.

responses.point: Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan would be a fair configuration (theory, first 2D experiment, first 3D materials), which leaves Mele out despite his central role in the theory.
responses.response: I take the 3D point seriously, but I disagree with the trade. Dropping Mele removes half of the theoretical origin in order to add a third experimental claim. Hasan's ARPES work is a further step in the story, and the 3D history also depends on Fu, Moore, Balents and Roy, who cannot be credited here, as Lindroth also notes. A citation about the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 classification is coherent and exactly matched to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. A prize that also tried to cover 3D materials would invite a more difficult attribution dispute.

responses.point: B013 is a strong atomic-physics case: Katori's magic-wavelength idea and Ye's record-accuracy realisations give about 1e-18 uncertainty, with a two-name attribution that is clean and fair.
responses.response: I agree that B013 has the cleanest attribution on the list, and its importance is unambiguous, which is why I ranked it fifth. My reservation is whether the committee sees an instrument refinement as a discovery, given the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes next to it. I accept that this argument is weaker than I first suggested. But under the three-person limit B013 cannot be combined with a three-person topological prize, and a combined prize would force a cut in B041 that I would not accept.

responses.point: The theta13 measurement is a decisive, clean precision result that opened the way to CP-violation searches, with Wang and Luk of Daya Bay and Nishikawa of T2K as the credited names.
responses.response: I respect the clarity of the measurement, but I have a serious qualification. As you note yourself, RENO and Double Chooz leaders could claim parity, and the reactor and accelerator streams are separate lines of discovery. It is hard to see from the supplied text that three names are a defensible allocation across three reactor experiments and T2K, and the entry has no opening support beyond your own ballot. I also think the 2015 oscillation prize already honoured the larger conceptual step, so the novelty relative to that award is lower than for topology.

uncertainties: Whether Hasan or Mele should hold the third slot, and how the committee weighs the omission of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Balents, which cannot be resolved from the supplied text.
Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize is felt to have already covered the area, which would weaken the case for B041.
Whether B029 (adding Xue's quantum anomalous Hall realisation) should be treated as a separate achievement or as part of the same story as B041.
My knowledge of the priority history is from recollection and has not been verified against sources.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile: none of the credited names for the shortlisted candidates appears among my documented collaborators or supervisors.
